name: Dragoevo

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay and Merlot sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Gewürztraminer is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely. Marl is a limy clay. It holds water and makes vines ripen later, which keeps acidity in the grapes. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
